security_audit.summary: The skill is not overtly malicious and I found no prompt injection attempt. It does handle a RollingGo API key and directs users to run mutable third-party CLI packages, so the main risks are credential exposure and supply-chain drift.

remediation.suggestion: Pin RollingGo package versions or checksums in examples, and publish an audited upgrade process instead of defaulting to @latest.

remediation.issue: API keys shown in command-line arguments
remediation.suggestion: Prefer per-skill environment secret injection or a secret manager. Remove --api-key examples or warn that command-line secrets can be logged.

remediation.issue: Broad host and sandbox credential scope
remediation.suggestion: Recommend per-skill secret scope as the default and clearly discourage host-wide or container-wide API key injection unless required.

remediation.issue: External command execution by an AI agent
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before installing, upgrading, or running RollingGo, especially when network access and credentials are involved.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Latest Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to run rollinggo@latest through npx or uvx and to upgrade installed tools before use. A future package release could change executed code without marketplace review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly prefer @latest and refresh or upgrade behavior in multiple files. This is a clear supply-chain risk even though it supports freshness.

semantic_findings.title: API Key In Command-Line Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The reference docs show using --api-key with placeholder secrets. Real API keys passed this way may be exposed through shell history, process listings, or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation repeatedly presents --api-key usage. The values are placeholders, but the recommended pattern creates a common secret exposure channel.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Host Secret Injection Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The host environment reference allows API key injection at host and sandbox configuration levels. Shared scopes can expose the same credential to more skills or containers than needed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly documents host-level and sandbox-level environment injection. The risk depends on host configuration, but the broad-scope guidance is explicit.

content.value_statement: Hotel search often needs current prices, tags, and room details. This skill uses RollingGo CLI to find hotels and compare structured results.
actual_capabilities: Search hotels by destination, dates, guests, star rating, budget, and distance.
Retrieve RollingGo hotel tags for preferred, required, or excluded filters.
Query hotel details, room options, prices, and refund policy information by hotel ID.
Compare candidate hotels using structured results from the CLI.
Return booking URLs or hotel detail links when they are present in results.
Use npm or uv based RollingGo execution paths.
limitations: Requires a RollingGo API key and network access.
Covers hotel search only, not flights, trains, transfers, or car rentals.
Availability and prices depend on the RollingGo service response.
Final booking happens outside the skill through returned links.

use_cases.title: Find Family Hotels Near Attractions
use_cases.description: Search hotels near a landmark with dates, guest counts, budget, and family-friendly tags.

use_cases.title: Compare Room Prices Before Booking
use_cases.description: Fetch hotel details and room prices for selected hotel IDs before sharing booking links.

use_cases.title: Build Filtered Hotel Shortlists
use_cases.description: Use tags, brands, distance, and star ratings to create a focused shortlist for a trip.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Hotel Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search by place and dates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for hotels near Tokyo Disney Resort for two adults from April 1 to April 3, 2026. Show five good options.

prompt_templates.title: Budget And Star Filter
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate filtering with price and quality constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find hotels near Shanghai Disney for two nights under 800 CNY per night. Limit results to four and five star hotels.

prompt_templates.title: Tag Based Family Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Use the tag library before searching.
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the available hotel tags, then search Tokyo Disney hotels that are family friendly and include breakfast.

prompt_templates.title: Detailed Hotel Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using search results and hotel detail lookups.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for three hotels near the Bund in Shanghai, inspect room details for each hotel ID, and compare price, room type, and cancellation policy.

output_examples.input: Find hotels near Tokyo Disney for two adults in early April.
output_examples.output: A ranked shortlist with hotel names, nightly prices, star ratings, distance, and available booking links.

output_examples.input: Compare details for selected hotel IDs.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of room types, total stay prices, refund terms, and reasons to choose each option.

output_examples.input: Find family friendly hotels with breakfast near Shanghai Disney.
output_examples.output: A filtered list using valid RollingGo tags, with notes about budget fit and distance from the destination.

best_practices: Confirm destination, dates, guests, rooms, and budget before searching.
Use hotel IDs from search results when requesting room details.
Store the RollingGo API key in a scoped secret configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for flights, trains, transfers, or rental cars.
Do not pass real API keys directly in prompts or visible command text.
Do not rely on hotel names when a hotel ID is available.

faq.question: What does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches hotels through the RollingGo CLI and can retrieve hotel details, tags, room prices, and booking links.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The RollingGo CLI needs a RollingGo API key through a scoped environment variable or another supported secret source.

faq.question: Can it complete a booking?
faq.answer: No. It can return booking URLs or hotel detail links, but the user completes payment outside the skill.

faq.question: Can it filter by hotel tags?
faq.answer: Yes. It can fetch valid tags and use them as preferred, required, or excluded hotel filters.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users verify before booking?
faq.answer: Users should verify price, dates, room type, cancellation policy, taxes, fees, and booking site terms.
